issues.legal_issue: Delivery of a signed arbitral award to a party’s advocate does not constitute delivery to the party for purposes of starting the limitation period for an application to set aside the award.
material_facts: A signed copy of the arbitral award was received by the respondent’s counsel, but was not then delivered to the respondent itself.
The respondent later obtained the signed award and filed its application to set it aside within three months of obtaining it.
The High Court held that service on counsel did not satisfy the requirement to deliver the award to the party, and the matter was brought before the Supreme Court by special leave.
issues.conclusion: Service of the signed award on the respondent’s counsel did not start the limitation period. The application was filed within time after the respondent itself obtained the award, so the objection that it was time-barred was rightly rejected and the special leave petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(h), 31(5), and 34(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, “party” means a party to the arbitration agreement, not that party’s agent or advocate. Proper delivery under Section 31(5) requires delivery of a signed copy of the award to the party itself, and the period under Section 34(3) runs from that delivery. This follows Union of India v. Tecco Trichy Engineers & Contractors and State of Maharashtra v. ARK Builders Pvt. Ltd. Pushpa Devi Bhagat v. Rajinder Singh concerned an advocate’s authority to act in proceedings and does not alter this requirement; Nilakantha Sidramappa Ningshetti v. Kashinath Somanna Ningashetti arose under the 1940 Act, which had no equivalent to Section 31(5).

rule.if: award_challenge_proceeding and signed_award_delivered_to_counsel and signed_award_not_yet_delivered_to_party and party_later_received_signed_award

predicates.award_challenge_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding to set aside an arbitral award.
predicates.signed_award_delivered_to_counsel: A signed copy of the award was delivered to the party’s advocate.
predicates.signed_award_not_yet_delivered_to_party: The signed copy had not been delivered to the party when it was delivered to the advocate.
predicates.party_later_received_signed_award: The party itself later received the signed copy of the award.
predicates.counsel_service_does_not_start_limitatio: Delivery of the signed award to an advocate, without delivery to the party, does not start the limitation period for challenging the award.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to set aside an arbitral award and the signed award is first delivered to its advocate rather than to the party, that delivery does not start the limitation period.
